faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Everything you need to know before checking your documents.
faq.ctaDescription: Try your first document check today.

documents.question: What documents can I check?
documents.answer: You can analyse rental contracts (Mietvertrag), annual service charge statements (Nebenkostenabrechnung), rent increase notices (Mietzinserhoehung), deposit deductions and landlord letters.

timing.question: How long does the analysis take?
timing.answer: Most documents are analysed within 1-3 minutes. Larger files may take slightly longer.

result.question: What do I receive after the analysis?
result.answer: You receive a detailed report including detected issues, explanations, recommendations and, where applicable, a draft letter you can send to your landlord.

legal.question: Is this legal advice?
legal.answer: No. Swiss Tenant Assistant provides informational analysis and recommendations. It does not replace advice from a qualified lawyer or tenant association.

security.question: Is my data secure?
security.answer: Yes. Documents are encrypted, processed securely and never shared with third parties. Access to reports is protected and time-limited.

pdf.question: Can I download a PDF report?
pdf.answer: Yes. Every completed analysis includes a professional PDF report that you can download and keep for your records.

letters.question: Can the platform generate letters for my landlord?
letters.answer: Yes. Swiss Tenant Assistant can generate letters for service charge disputes, repair requests, deposit return requests and other common tenant situations.

serious.question: What if the platform finds a serious issue?
serious.answer: The report will explain the issue and suggest next steps. For complex legal situations, we recommend contacting a lawyer or tenant association.

subscription.question: Do I need a subscription?
subscription.answer: No. You only pay for the checks you need. There are no recurring subscription fees.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: This page explains how Swiss Tenant Assistant may collect, use, and protect information when a user uploads documents, creates an account, or purchases a workflow.

sections.title: What we collect
sections.body: We may collect account details, uploaded tenancy documents, payment metadata, support messages, and technical logs required to operate the service.

sections.title: How we use data
sections.body: We use submitted data to authenticate users, run document extraction, generate reports or letters, process payments, prevent abuse, and improve reliability.

sections.title: Storage and retention
sections.body: Documents and related records may be stored for the period needed to deliver the workflow, keep audit history, resolve disputes, and comply with legal obligations.

sections.title: Processors and infrastructure
sections.body: Some processing may rely on hosting, email, payment, OCR, or AI providers. Final production policy must list each provider and the legal basis for those transfers.

sections.title: User rights
sections.body: Users should be able to request access, correction, deletion, or export of their personal data, subject to retention and compliance requirements.

terms.title: Terms
terms.intro: These terms describe the intended rules for access to Swiss Tenant Assistant and for use of its document review and tenant communication workflows.

sections.title: Service scope
sections.body: The product is a narrow software workflow for tenancy document handling, issue spotting, and draft generation. It is not a law firm and does not create an attorney-client relationship.

sections.title: Accounts and access
sections.body: Users are responsible for account credentials, lawful use of the service, and accuracy of the information they upload or submit.

sections.title: Payments and paid outputs
sections.body: Certain checks, reports, or letters may require payment before access is granted. Refund and billing rules should be finalized before launch.

sections.title: Availability
sections.body: The service may change, pause, or be unavailable during maintenance, updates, or technical incidents. No uninterrupted availability is guaranteed.

sections.title: Liability limits
sections.body: Final terms should define liability exclusions, permitted use, governing law, and dispute handling in line with the jurisdiction where the service is offered.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.intro: This page explains the intended boundaries of product output and the review expected from users before they rely on generated findings, summaries, or draft letters.

sections.title: No legal advice
sections.body: Outputs are informational software results and draft materials. They should not be presented as legal advice, legal representation, or a substitute for qualified counsel.

sections.title: No guarantee of completeness
sections.body: Document extraction, OCR, rule checks, and AI-generated text can miss facts, misread source material, or produce incomplete recommendations.

sections.title: User review required
sections.body: Users remain responsible for reviewing source documents, checking deadlines and figures, and deciding whether professional legal review is necessary.

sections.title: Third-party dependencies
sections.body: Service quality may depend on external providers used for storage, email, payment, OCR, or AI processing. Interruptions or defects in those services can affect results.
